reason: Reproduced through the real UI and confirmed in pixels, not only in geometry. From owner-flight I opened 'Send the invitations' and pressed the editor's own -7 once, then 'Final dress fitting' and pressed -7 three times: three moments land on Sat 1 Aug (data-stack lead/follow/follow, data-crowded true on both followers). place() gives a follower gap=1, so the next plate's copy top is exactly 1px under the previous copy's bottom, and .b-item[data-crowded=true] .b-copy paints box-shadow 0 0 0 12px var(--back) - opaque #ffffff on paper, #111111 on ink - which is outside its own border box and, being later in DOM order in the same stacking context with no z-index anywhere, paints OVER the previously painted sibling. Through Preview (the guest surface, desk at 1440 and phone at 390) the follower's .b-copy has no bottom padding and .b-grab is absent, so dateBottom == copyBottom exactly (slack 0.00px, against 12px on the lead and 44px on the owner's rows), and the halo top lands 10.19px at 1440 / 10.78px at 390 ABOVE the date's baseline box. Screenshotted the cluster at dsf=2 on both grounds: the middle row's 'Sat 1 Aug' is guillotined - roughly the top 5px of a 15.4px line box survives as disconnected glyph tops ('S t 1 A' fragments) with nothing below. Identical on ?v=paper and ?v=ink, at 1440 and 390. Neither gate sees it: interaction-check.mjs:2876 asserts only 'a stacked pair does not overlap on the render that forms it' with gap > 0 - and the gap IS 1px, positive, so the assertion passes while the paint does not; the clipping check at :142 looks for hidden overflow, not for an opaque shadow spread over a neighbour. Nothing in SETTLED.md covers it (row-plate-crosses-the-right-margin is a horizontal-margin argument, not paint order). Two corrections to the finding, neither of which touches its substance: (1) it is WRONG about the owner plan - there .b-grab sits below the date inside .b-copy, so the follower's slack is 32px and the date is fully painted; what the halo eats on the owner is the bottom ~10px of the Edit control's box, which erases that control's hairline underline (the one thing b.css says 'declares it a control at rest') on every middle row, a milder but real second symptom on the same line of CSS. (2) 'silent content deletion' overstates it: the day is stated identically on the lead row two lines above, so no unique fact is lost - what the guest gets is a half-guillotined line of mono type, which at a 9.5 bar against Linear/Stripe is a plain rendering defect, not a taste call. Real, and cheap to fix.
sharpenedFix: Exactly the finding's fix, verified at runtime on both grounds: give the follower the bottom padding the lead already has - .b-item[data-stack="follow"] .b-copy { border-top: 1px solid var(--fore-16); padding-top: var(--gap-snug); padding-bottom: var(--gap-snug); } (b.css:328-331). Injected into the driven three-on-a-day and re-measured: every follower's slack goes 0px -> 12px, the halo top falls 1px below the previous copy's bottom edge (same 1px margin the lead already relies on), and all three 'Sat 1 Aug' lines render whole on paper and on ink at 1440 and 390. It also restores the middle row's Edit underline on the owner plan (grab bottom moves from copyBottom to copyBottom-12, clear of the halo), so one declaration closes both symptoms. The stack's push arithmetic derives from measured copy heights and reflows on its own - measured stack height grows 12px per follower, nothing else in the composition moves. Then add the gate assertion the finding asks for, but assert PAINT, not gap: for a run of three or more on one day, require every non-last row's dateBottom to sit at least 12px above the next row's copy top (i.e. copyBottom - dateBottom >= the crowded halo spread), since the existing gap > 0 test passes at 1px and cannot ever catch this.
